note: Never served. The cold rep checks and the journey (bun run journey) send these as the learner's answer to a cold rep on card A. The wrong one fails on any problem of the skill; the right one passes on any, because it says what to do in each common case.
wrong: git stash undoes the last commit. I'd run git stash, and the commit comes off the branch so I can redo it.
right:
It depends on whether the commit is pushed, and which commit it is. HEAD~1 below means the last commit: HEAD~N takes off the last N instead (HEAD~3 for three), and origin/main takes off every commit I haven't pushed, so git reset origin/main (or --soft, or --hard) makes the branch match the remote again.
Not pushed, the last commit (or last few), and I want to keep the changes: git reset HEAD~1 undoes it and leaves its changes in my files, unstaged; git reset --soft HEAD~1 leaves them staged instead.
Not pushed, the last commit (or last few), and I want the changes gone too: git reset --hard HEAD~1.
Not pushed, and the commit to undo is an older one, with newer commits on top that must stay: git rebase -i <hash>~1, where <hash> is that commit's, and change its line from pick to drop. The newer commits stay, and the branch looks as if that commit was never made. (git revert <hash> also works, adding a new commit that undoes it.)
Already pushed or shared with others: don't rewrite history. git revert <hash> makes a new commit that undoes that commit, even an older one with newer commits on top (git revert HEAD for the last one), then git push.
Pushed, but only to my own branch that nobody else has pulled, and I want it gone from the remote too: the same reset as for an unpushed commit (git reset HEAD~1 keeps the changes unstaged, --soft keeps them staged, --hard drops them), then git push --force-with-lease.
Only the message, the author, or the files of the last commit were wrong, and it isn't pushed: fix the files, git add them (git rm --cached for one that shouldn't be in it), then git commit --amend (with --author="Name <email>" for the author).
Committed on the wrong branch, such as main, and not pushed, and I want the work on another branch and this one back as it was: git branch <name> makes the new branch at this commit, keeping the work; then git reset --hard HEAD~1 on the wrong branch (HEAD~N for N commits, or origin/main to match the remote again); then git switch <name>. For a branch that already exists: git switch to it and git cherry-pick <hash>, then the same reset on the wrong branch. To carry the changes over uncommitted instead: git reset HEAD~1 (or git reset origin/main for every unpushed commit; --soft keeps them staged), then git switch -c <name> (git switch <name> for an existing one) and commit there.
